title: Looking for any “smart” glasses that support hearing aid or real time closed caption through the glasses : r/deaf
text:
r/deaf
 2y ago 

u/RichieEB

# Looking for any “smart” glasses that support hearing aid or real time closed caption through the glasses

Technology

I know that So far we don’t have the best technology reliability of these glasses but they do work but I’m wondering if any of those that own one of various brands which to go for. I’m always missing out in my friend conversations so I don’t bother even trying to listen to every single word while I’m trying my best to lip read at the same time.

I don’t want to use a transcribe app through phone, this idea with the glasses have been with me since I was a kid and only now it’s starting to become a reality. Let me know any recommendations would be greatly appreciated. English isn’t the best

You're looking for something like Google Glasses which launched and crashed about 2012-14.

You could buy one of the later versions mentioned in this article https://screenrant.com/google-glass-smart-glasses-what-happened-explained/ - some of them are available cheaper used - and see if you can use them for live transcription.

Google is just about to launch a new version of their glasses later this year, so you could wait for that.

But you know what: **It's going to suck.**

Will be expensive, microphone won't be good, activating the transcribe will be annoying or fiddly, battery life will suck, using the transcript itself will be annoying ie the words will lag the speech and it will only show you a few words at a time.

Pretty much the best AI transcription you can get right now is with a high-end smart phone, with good microphones (or an external high quality microphone) and plenty of processing power / good 5g connection and a decent screen to see it on.

Smart glasses won't have any of that.

I suggest practicing just whipping your phone out quickly and activating AI transcription - put the icon on your home screen. Otter.ai is a well regarded app.

If that doesn't transcribe accurately, anything in a pair of glasses will be even worse.

Aluminautical


 2y ago

If OP does glasses or phone (that perhaps displays on glasses), the number-one thing to improve caption quality is a microphone on the other person -- like a clip-on bluetooth mic. The number-two thing is having that person watch the resulting captions, and improve their diction/enunciation to improve the software's accuracy. Both require effort, but are not impossible...

Clearly ASL exists for a very good reason, and helping friends learn it is a good thing.

Greybush\_The\_Rotund


 2y ago

Yeah it’s gonna be just more of the same, and I say this as someone who owns multiple pairs of these glasses (XRAI AR One, HearView, TranscribeGlass, several XREAL display glasses, a Vufine+ monocular display, and a Trivisio Junior monocular display).

If you’re not satisfied with the experience on your phone, it won’t be any better in the glasses because…a lot of them do the exact same thing (run an app on your phone to do the heavy lifting) and the only difference is seeing the words in your glasses versus seeing the words on your phone.

So, you’d just be paying hundreds of dollars for the ability to make partial eye contact with whoever you’re talking to, at best.

None of the glasses I’ve tried have apps that provide as good a user experience as plain old Google Live Transcribe on a phone. They’re all either missing something or pack in too many unnecessary extra features that add nothing of value, or the UX has more friction than Google Live Transcribe.

RichieEB

I mean I’d prefer to see it through the glasses than my phone so it’s not as noticeable

Greybush\_The\_Rotund


 2y ago

That’s the main reason I use them, I’m in so many meetings with hearing people that me staring into my phone makes me look disengaged.

Out of the ones I’ve tried, TranscribeGlass has the fewest pain points and the least friction. Not perfect, but it’s a lot cheaper than HearView and less fragile.

If you want an immediate noticeable increase in transcription quality, get a good external mic. Right now I’m using a Hollyland Lark M2S, and that’s a good one. Fair warning:  most of the cheap mics on Amazon will likely be so-so and probably not better than your phone’s built in mic, or slightly better at best. It’s worth investing in an actually good one.

Also, a lot of the experience involves managing your environment and making sure you’re in reasonably quiet places and that people aren’t talking over each other constantly, and avoiding situations where you’re in the middle of several overlapping conversations because the transcriber will not be able to focus *just* on the one you’re interested in.
